parsed.explanation: Thin data, but structural signals extrapolate toward severe risk, not midpoint. The dossier documents an actively enforced criminalisation regime (regular prosecutions of LGBTQ people in government areas, up to life imprisonment per one source, three months–three years per others), a death penalty under sharia in insurgent-controlled areas with documented killings by armed groups of alleged gay men as recently as 2024, deep societal stigma with no public discussion in any region, near-total absence of community infrastructure, and impunity. For a visibly gender-nonconforming visitor, the criminalised lever is precisely the kind used against gender-nonconforming people (rule 2: enforcement practice matters). This matches the 0.15 anchors: organised targeting plus state criminalisation with no recourse and no documented relief. No trans-specific provisions exist, but nothing in the record suggests protection; the same religious and state machinery targets those outside gender norms. The unresolved penalty range and absence of enforcement data do not soften the documented killing pattern.
